title: Smooth-bucket regulator with kernel-affinity and KV-cache sticky scoring
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Introduces a smooth-bucket regulator that reduces padding-induced waste and prefers kernel-aligned cohorts; improves cost and p95 latency for typical RAG and chat workloads.
description: Motivation: observed tail spikes when aggressive length bucketing created narrow bins that oscillated in occupancy across seconds, causing padding variability and kernel inefficiencies. This PR introduces a "smooth-bucket regulator" heuristic that (1) adds temporal smoothing to bucket boundaries to avoid rapid oscillation, (2) integrates a lightweight kernel-affinity estimator so cohorts favor kernels with better throughput for the predominant sequence lengths, and (3) biases placement for requests with warm KV cache to stay in the same cohort (sticky KV affinity) to reduce KV cache churn. The changes are implemented inside the continuous batch composer and scheduling layer; the feature is opt-in behind runtime config 'smooth_bucket_regulator=true' and a guardrail param 'max_boundary_shift_ms'. Implementation summary: we add a BucketRegulator object that maintains per-batcher histogram windows, computes smoothed boundary deltas with an exponential moving average, then rebalances requests into neighbor buckets only when smoothed benefit outweighs reallocation cost (estimated padding reduction minus kernel-switch overhead). Kernel affinity scores are derived from a mini cost-table populated by microbenchmarks run at boot and periodically updated; KV-stickiness adds a small positive score when request metadata indicates a populated KV handle. Benchmarks: internal perf run on c6g.4xlarge-equivalent with Llama2-7B-quantized profile; workloads: mixed chat (50%), short queries (30%), RAG retrieval+answer (20%) simulated from production traces. Results: median token throughput +3.8%, average token cost -6.7%, p95 latency improvement 12% on heavy RAG mixes, padding tokens reduced by ~18% overall for the trace set. Safety & fallbacks: when kernel-affinity table is stale or reports high variance we fallback to classic fixed bucketing; regulator exposes diagnostic metrics (regulator.bucket_shifts, regulator.kernel_mismatch_rate, regulator.kv_stick_hits) surfaced to the console. Tests and CI: unit tests for regulator boundary math and score composition, e2e smoke with continuous batch composer harness and a new micro-benchmark that asserts no regression in cold-start latency. Rolling strategy: merge to main with feature gate off by default; enable in canary pool #5 then progressively to Dedicated pools. Related: this complements ENG-6210 (KV cache eviction smoothing) and supersedes some ad-hoc heuristics introduced in earlier PRs. See commits for implementation notes and small refactors of the batch composer module.

review_comments: Mateo: Can you quantify the kernel-switch overhead used in the scoring? Author: we measured ~0.6-1.2ms overhead for model variants on our quantized kernels and use a conservative 1.5ms penalty (configurable).
Priya: I see potential for inflating bucket counts in pathological traces; suggest a hard cap per-bucket size. Author: added max_bucket_capacity and fallback to merge with neighbor when exceeded.
Jordan: tests are good but the e2e perf run had one flaky seed; re-ran and included deterministic seeding in tests.
Ops: please ensure metrics names here follow the console convention; updated registrations.yaml accordingly.
notes_on_deploy: Feature gate off by default. To try in canary set runtime.smooth_bucket_regulator=true and adjust runtime.sbr.max_boundary_shift_ms=200. Monitor regulator.bucket_shifts and kernel_mismatch_rate for first 24h.
observability_changes: Added exporter hooks for three new metrics and a small dashboard in the console for regulator health.
notes_for_release_manager: Non-breaking optimization; include note about opt-in gate and suggested canary rollout. Add to release notes under 'runtime: batching' with a short summary and benchmark numbers.
customer_impact: Low risk when gate is off; when enabled expects improved cost and tail latency for mixed-length workloads, especially RAG-heavy customers.
attribution: Design: Ava Chen and Mateo Ruiz. Implementation: Ava Chen, Priya Singh. Benchmarks: Jordan Lee. Reviews: infra and SRE teams.
notes_on_security: No new surface area. Any kernel calibration data is local to the node and not exported by default.
changelog_summary: Introduce Smooth-bucket regulator: temporal smoothing of length buckets, kernel-affinity scoring, and KV-cache stickiness to reduce padding and tail latency.
ui_changes: Added a toggle in the runtime section of Console and a small per-batcher metric panel.
test_plan: Unit tests for regulator math, integration test against continuous composer harness, perf regression gated via benchmark job. Deterministic seeding in tests to avoid flakiness.
notes_for_support: If customers report increased p50/p95 after enabling, check kernel_mismatch_rate and regulator.bucket_shifts; disable gate if mismatch_rate>0.2 and open ENG-xxxx for follow-up.
estimated_risks: Medium: scoring miscalibration could cause small regressions in edge traces; mitigated by conservative penalties and fallback to legacy bucketing.
hotfix_rollback_plan: Flip runtime.smooth_bucket_regulator=false and purge regulator state; no schema changes required.
local_testing_instructions: Run pytest services/runtime/batching/tests::test_bucket_regulator and run infra/benchmarks/run_sbr_bench.py with sample trace; use --seed for determinism.
acknowledgements: Thanks to infra perf team for the microbenchmark harness and SRE for canary guidance.
